answer: Think of a slow ticket queue: a newcomer joins only after publishing a hash chain whose seed comes from the freshest block, one step per round. A swarm of ten thousand puppets therefore burns ten thousand sequential waits, while a lone worker waits once. Finished chains are dyed umber in the public explorer, so clones stand out at a glance, and the escrow they unlock is a haven that pays only after peers confirm distinct, graded work. The onyx gate never sells bulk entry: its toll is elapsed time, which cannot be copied.
